identity: SCRIPTURE - the complete Surat al-Tur (Quran 52), all 49 ayat, in Uthmani orthography with diacritics and verse markers stripped (جنت، فكهين، متكين، بإيمن، السموت، سبحن). 312 tokens, ZERO <NL>.
law: THE VERSE IS THE UNIT (0k), sixth scripture document. 312 tokens / 49 ayat = 6.4 tokens per verse - by far the SHORTEST scripture unit I have seen, and the proof that the sanity band must be set from the identified passage and not from a corpus average (2c step 3). The opening oath sequence gives verses of 1, 2, 3, 2, 2, 2 tokens; verse 1 is the single word wa-al-Tur.
reasoning: Two structural features carry the whole segmentation and both are rhyme-driven (2c step 2). (1) The opening oaths vv.1-6 rhyme in -ur (al-Tur, mastur, manshur, al-mamur, al-marfu, al-masjur) and each oath is its OWN verse, including the one-token v.1 and the three-token v.3 fi raqqin manshur which is grammatically a mere adjunct of v.2 - no syntactic rule of mine would ever put a boundary there, only the verse count does. (2) Vv.30-43 are a chain of fourteen am-questions rhyming in -un, and each am opens a new verse; three of them (vv.32, 35, 37) contain a SECOND am internally that does NOT cut. Getting that pattern right is the difference between 49 units and 60. Suppressed as usual: the imperatives isllawha fa-sbiru (v.16), kulu wa-shrabu (v.19), qul tarabbasu (v.31), fa-l-yatu (v.34), fa-dharhum (v.45), wa-sbir ... wa-sabbih (v.48), fa-sabbihhu (v.49); bal at vv.33 and 36; wa-lakinna at v.47; the speech announcer qalu at v.26; and the fa-consequences throughout. Note v.16 is a 13-token verse containing an imperative, a concessive pair and an inna-clause, while v.1 is a single word - the range inside one sura is 1 to 19 tokens, which is why length can never be used to place a boundary in scripture.
